claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
The reported HfNbTiVAl10 state contains multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A transfer-learning/active-learning model trained on small compositional variations around HfNbTiVAl10 can reliably predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
Key compositional descriptors and short-range-order parameters are sufficient model inputs for capturing the relevant property variation.
The model is intended for room-temperature tensile and fracture-test conditions.
The multilevel chemical fluctuations and hierarchical heterostructure mediate the mechanical responses of HfNbTiVAl10.
Correlated compositional descriptors can indirectly capture the mechanical effects of the hierarchical heterostructure and chemical fluctuations.
A focused, compositionally tuned dataset allows the model to bypass full-scale first-principles and CALPHAD calculations.
Learning correlations between slight compositional adjustments and emergent mechanical properties enables rapid property prediction with less computational work.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness with an approximate 10% error margin.
The proposed model will reduce computational time by at least fivefold relative to full-scale CALPHAD or first-principles computations.
Prior full-CALPHAD, extensive ab initio, and high-dimensional machine-learning approaches typically have error margins of approximately 25–30% for the relevant predictions.
Prior approaches require significantly greater computational resources than the proposed focused model.
Significant alteration of the hierarchical microstructure can break the correlation between the selected descriptors and mechanical properties.
Unexpected phase transitions or processing-induced disorder can make the model unreliable.
Compositions outside the model's training regime can make its predictions unreliable.
The proposed 10% error and fivefold efficiency targets depend on the representativeness of the training dataset.
